text: The Dependencies sheet of the Service Story Catalog v1 is the source of the v5 graph, and the template baseline of DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 is stated once on the Dependency classes sheet instead of being repeated as a row on every non-CON story.
why: The catalog and the story files of the same run differ by 75 template rows on ten stories, and a map that repeated seven contracts on all 746 non-CON stories would be unreadable and would not match the published catalog.
read: Service Story Catalog v1, Dependencies sheet; story files behind _work/msr/fragments; Template and Rules R5.5 (DP table) and R5.7
applied_in: Dependency classes sheet, section The service template baseline; Story dependencies v5 note rows; Read me
impact: No story, lane or date changes. The map shows 2,534 rows and states the baseline rule once, so a reader knows every non-CON story also takes the seven template contracts.

text: The five version 4 dependencies that no v5 row carries stay visible in the Legacy dependency trace with status Not carried and add no row to the graph.
why: No source gives a row between those pairs, and the four new stories involved are an OPS story and two QA harness stories whose work starts from the platform template on Day 1.
read: Legacy dependency trace sheet; Service Story Catalog v1, Dependencies sheet; Template and Rules R6
applied_in: Legacy dependency trace sheet, rows RWB-E1-056, RWB-TE-009 and RWB-TE-010
impact: The four stories keep their catalog Ready value and nothing in the plan moves. A later version adds an X row if the OPS run books or a harness really waits for the named story.

text: Class X stays on the ten rows that point at RWB-PLT-TE001-APP and RWB-PLT-TE012-APP: platform technical-enabler work is team-type work even when its work type is App development.
why: Template and Rules R5.4 gives H only to the same service or a platform CON story and C only to another service's CON story, so X is the only class that records the row without making it block a build.
read: Service Story Catalog v1, Stories and Dependencies sheets; Template and Rules R5.3, R5.4
applied_in: Dependency classes sheet, check row X; Story dependencies v5 rows of the ten stories
impact: The ten rows are tracked and never block. The class counts are H 1,600, C 440, I 412, X 82.

text: The five Wave 0 dependencies of Architecture v5 slide 39 stay on the Dependency classes sheet exactly as slide 39 states them, and no new DEP ID is created in this version.
why: The version 4 external table stops at DEP-36, and issuing DEP-37 to DEP-41 here would create IDs in a family another document owns before its next version is written.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 38 and 39; Recovery Workbench Dependency Map v4, Dependencies sheet

confirm: Program manager with the solution architect
impact: The five dependencies are visible with their slide 39 owner roles and are raised as P1 in the gap register. The next version of the Risks Assumptions Issues and Dependencies document takes them as DEP-37 to DEP-41.

text: The 124 non-CON stories that carry no dependency row keep the Ready value of the catalog and take only the template baseline.
why: The OPS, INF, DB and ITG stories are the other team types' own work and the 31 application stories have no dependency beyond the template contracts, so the catalog lists no row for them.
read: Service Story Catalog v1, Stories and Dependencies sheets; Template and Rules R5.5, R5.7
applied_in: Read me, The graph in numbers; Dependency classes sheet, section The service template baseline
impact: None of the 124 stories is re-cut and no lane changes. A story that turns out to have a real in-lane dependency gets the row in its own story file first.

text: The Dependency Map v5 is issued in Draft: no approval of the version 4 map or of this version is recorded in the sources.
why: The run has no approval step and the D-RCV-60 overlay says to record an assumption and continue in Draft status.
read: Version 4 workbook and its properties; the read-only sources of this work package
applied_in: Read me, A7 and the change log; every sheet of this version
impact: The four classes and the 2,534 rows are used as the plan of record inside the run, and the document carries Status Draft until a later approval.

text: The version 4 sheet is kept unchanged and renamed Story dependencies v4, and Story dependencies v5 is the live graph.
why: Template and Rules R8.2 never edits an existing file and R8.7 asks for the next version; keeping both leaves the 325 legacy rows readable next to the 2,534 new ones and gives the Legacy dependency trace something to trace from.
read: Recovery Workbench Dependency Map v4, Story dependencies sheet; Template and Rules R8.2, R8.7
applied_in: Sheet Story dependencies v4 (kept, renamed); sheet Story dependencies v5; Read me
impact: Any reader or tracker that reads the old sheet name finds it once renamed; the realigned graph is one sheet to its right.

text: The Needed by dates of the 36 external dependencies are dependency dates, copied from version 4 unchanged, and are not marked tentative.
why: Template and Rules R10 marks release dates tentative and no release date appears on any sheet of this document; marking a dependency date tentative would change a value the source states plainly.
